director.chapterArc: Negotiation from threat; establishing terms through tactical competence rather than force.
director.restraintNote: Maintain a grounded, observational tone throughout. The Ember reveal is delivered with flat factual boredom, not wonder. Callie's internal calculations are rhythmic and precise, never panicked until the final existential question about 'the words'.

cues.delivery: Observational clarity. Describe the ambush setup as a tactical fact: worst place for an attack, best for visibility.
cues.from: "They picked this on purpose," her mother said. "Look where they've stopped."
cues.through: They had stopped in the worst possible place for an ambush and the best possible place to be seen from. The road ran straight and open for that whole quarter mile with the cut wall on one side and the flat on the other, and the wagon was drawn up square across it with the canvas rolled back, and the team was out of the traces and hobbled — a mule and a horse, which was a thing Callie had never seen anybody do on purpose — and all four people were sitting on the ground on the near side of the wagon where Callie could count them from where she stood. There was a fire. There was a pot on it. There was nowhere for a fifth person to be hiding within four hundred paces and they had arranged it so that this was obvious.
cues.reason: Establishing the scene's geometry and Callie's assessment of safety.

cues.delivery: Flat delivery for Katori. Introduce the group with 'fence post' stability; no emotional spikes.
cues.from: "Then here." The woman stood. She did it without pushing off anything, straight up out of a cross-legged sit, and Callie noticed that and filed it. "My name is Katori. That's Pell, who drives. Ines, who shoots. Otto, who lifts."
cues.through: "Callie," Katori said. She was maybe thirty-five. She was a head shorter than Callie's mother and she stood the way a fence post stands. She had a grey knitted cap pushed back off her forehead, and a flat, unhurried face, and she looked at Callie the way Callie had looked at the sprung snare. "We watched you last night. All four of us, for about half an hour. I want that said out loud before anything else, because you saw us and you'll have been chewing on it since, and I'd rather you chewed on the true version."
cues.reason: Character introduction via Callie's lens of tactical observation.

cues.delivery: Tactical precision. Katori asks about the 'ten minutes' with curiosity but no drama; Callie answers with arithmetic clarity.
cues.from: "A girl came up the drainage about an hour before dark with a hook on her shoulder and went straight to the culvert without slowing down, which told me she'd decided on it from somewhere back. She spent a while at the mouth of it on her hands and knees and we couldn't see what she was doing." Katori's eyes went across Callie's face without any hurry. "That's the part I want. Not the killing. Everybody on this road can kill something once. What was the ten minutes?"
cues.through: "I cut a step in the silt so I'd have a back foot," she said. "I put my coat on the rebar in the crown so I'd know where it was without looking. I paced the gap between the wall and where a big one would stand, because that's how I was coming out."
cues.reason: Demonstrating competence through specific physical details.

cues.delivery: Expository clarity. Pell's explanation of the map and causeway is dry data; Katori's voice remains flat.
cues.from: "We're going to Meridian," Katori said. "We've come up from the Warren country in the south-east, which is a long way from here and looks nothing like here. We have freight, and I'd rather not say what, and you'd rather not know. Pell."
cues.through: "That's us," Pell said, tapping. "That's the rail grade you saw us on. And that — " he moved the pencil an inch north and stopped it on a long blue shape with a pale line drawn across the waist of it — "is where our information ends and our guessing starts. Because the book says there's a reservoir there with a two-mile causeway over the middle of it, and the book was printed in a year when everything worked, and the book does not know about any of the last sixty years."

cues.delivery: Negotiation stance. Callie's offer of information is a transaction; Katori's hiring pitch is matter-of-fact.
cues.from: "It'll take a wagon. It won't take a wagon and anything coming the other way, because it's one wide and there's no turning on it." Callie stopped. She had not meant to give them that much and it had come out anyway, and she understood, a beat too late, that this was exactly what her mother had meant about silences. "That's free," she said. "I'm not selling you that."
cues.through: "I want to hire you to Meridian. Two things. You walk the road ahead of us and you tell us what you told me just then, every day, before we get to it instead of after. And when something comes at this wagon you stand at the back of it with that hook and you do what you did last night." She held up one finger. "That's the whole job. I am not hiring a soldier and I don't want one. I have three people who can hold a line. I do not have one who can look at a bent thistle and tell me where a husk line runs."
cues.reason: Shifting from threat to business arrangement.

cues.delivery: The Ember reveal. Katori's demonstration is casual; her explanation of the 'One shape' mechanic must be delivered with flat factual boredom.
cues.from: The crate Pell was sitting on had a lid nailed down and a bad corner, and while the rest of it was going on he had got off it and got a bar under the lid and was working at it without much success. He made a noise of complaint. Katori put her hand out, palm down, over the crate, and did not look away from Callie while she did it.
cues.through: "One shape," said Katori. "That shape. I've had it eleven years and it's one shape, and it does that, and on a bad day it doesn't do that either." She said it without any weight on it at all, the way you'd report the weather. "That's what it is. It's a tool that lives in your chest instead of your belt. Anybody who tells you it's more than that is selling you a cord to wear it on."

cues.delivery: Assertive negotiation. Callie demands the wagon for her mother; Katori accepts without surprise.
cues.through: "I know what people do." She turned and started for the mules, and stopped, and said, without turning around: "Pell will want your terms in the book. Say them to him the way you said them to me. Don't help him by making them smaller."
cues.reason: Establishing the new dynamic and hierarchy.

cues.delivery: Reflective closure. Callie's internal state is one of uncertainty; Katori's final words are delivered with a hint of dry wisdom.
cues.from: Callie walked. She walked out ahead of the traces where Katori put her, thirty or forty paces up, close enough to be shouted to and far enough to be useful, and she found within the first mile that she had no idea what to do with her hands. She had pulled something every day since the spring. Her chest ached where the strapping wasn't.
cues.through: She walked on ahead, and Callie stood for a second in the middle of the road with the flat grey country going north in front of her, and then went after her, and did not ask the next question, because she had a strong sense that the answer to it was waiting for her somewhere up the road regardless of whether she asked.
cues.reason: Ending on the subtext of 'the words' and future anxiety.

There was a fire. There was a pot on it. There was nowhere for a fifth person to be hiding within four hundred paces and they had arranged it so that this was obvious.
pauses.reason: Scene reset after establishing the ambush geometry.

pauses.reason: Completed thought on tactical preparation; pause for Katori's reaction.
Emphasis on the specific tactical action.

pauses.before: it was eleven minutes before dark
pauses.reason: Precise time measurement as a fact of observation.

pauses.after: "No," Katori agreed. "You're not. You just did."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Callie realizes she gave information away freely.

pauses.before: fight a husk in a hole in the ground with a farm tool
pauses.reason: Contrast between violence and mundane tools.

pauses.after: Then her hand was empty again. There was a flat grey slab in it, about the size of her palm, three fingers thick, rounded at the corners. She turned it over once and put it in her coat.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing; the silence of the Ember reveal and Callie's breathlessness.

pauses.after: "How much of that can you do?" she said finally.
pauses.reason: Pause for Katori to deliver the flat explanation of her power.

pauses.before: It's a tool that lives in your chest instead of your belt
pauses.reason: Clarification of the Ember mechanic against expectation.

pauses.before: My mother rides. Not when it's bad.
pauses.reason: Emphasis on the condition and necessity of the demand.

pauses.after: "You're not," Callie said, and did not turn around, and kept her eyes on Katori, and found it took everything she had.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on Callie's internal struggle; transition to agreement.

pauses.after: "I like her enormously," Pell said. "That's a separate column."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Pell's dry commentary on the horse.
